dimensions.evidence: Observed dictionary24, original shared-shape arena113, receiver20 and cache24 bytes on both host compilers. Keys and values are distinct typed arrays; original shape index is separate from property count.

Dictionary owns four keys/values per object. Shared model uses one113-byte arena plus20 per receiver and optional24 per cache. Compare common admitted layouts; dictionary has no16-transition exhaustion, and no equality of capacity contracts is claimed.

Zero initialization admits empty dictionary; copied scalar fields need no external roots or destructors. Generic/cached receiver and shape arena must remain live throughout access; cached owner is borrowed.

Dictionary deletion shifts key/value pairs together. Existing updates work at count4. Direct generic access reads current receiver layout and current field; independent outputs do not alias input/control storage.

No dynamic allocation in these typed kernels. Dictionary creates no shared transitions; original shape set can exhaust16 metadata rows while common admitted lookup traces remain comparable. Host tools allocate independently.
Delete shifts at most3 pairs and clears one trailing pair. Shared shape updates change a receiver index and copy four-key metadata only on new transitions. Neither lookup copies whole objects.

Dropping these scalar-only controls is constant lifetime termination with no callback. Dictionary erase is bounded shifting, not an external-resource destructor; a future owning payload must supply explicit move/drop and rollback.

Direct lookup performs at most4 key comparisons without a cache. Original cache checks up to2 guarded pairs and switches to sticky generic on a third distinct pair. Actual disassembly is recorded; functions are separate translation units without LTO.

These operations require serialized ownership. No atomic data-race repair is implied by generic lookup or immutable descriptors. The broader family TSan covers its distinct foreign-reader schedule only.

Full new insertion and absent deletion preserve dictionary; missing lookup preserves output777. Four compiled mutants reject false full-capacity rejection, mispaired deletion, wrong-layout lookup and overwritten missing output. Independent38880 dictionary observations and generic/cached update traces passed.

Six actual compiler/optimization configurations have clean, unchanged and single-header rebuild logs. O2 seconds clean/no-change/header: GCC0.7658/0.0507/0.6935; Clang0.6319/0.0659/0.5062. Process/filesystem noise prevents general compiler ranking.

Whole probe O2 text/data/BSS: GCC11936/616/16, Clang14763/600/16. Generic versus cached local frames: GCC8/32, Clang0/16 bytes. Dictionary set/delete/get frames: GCC8/8/8, Clang0/48/0. Baseline functions are linked; these are local compiler observations, not all-call-stack bounds.

540 retained equal-contract samples plus36 discarded warmups,10000 calls each; one/two/three layouts, missing every17th and same-layout update every13th. Python independently checks checksums, statuses and exact cache counters. Setup excluded; observer/loop/check overhead included. No hardware cache counter, physical, JIT or learner claim.

sealed_decision.choice: Keep an explicit direct path and dictionary alternative; choose based on admitted mutation/shape reuse rather than assume cache wins.
sealed_decision.counterexample: Three alternating shape/key pairs make the original cache sticky generic; deleting one dictionary key shifts offsets so a stale offset is not a valid cached handler.
